wiki_search_description: Find a page by its title or one of its headings.
wiki_status_partly_built: This is partly built: some of what this page describes isn't in the app yet.
wiki_status_planned: This is planned: what this page describes isn't in the app yet.
wiki_demo_off: One-click demo sign-in is switched off on this server.
wiki_live_diagram: A change travels from the server, through the log and the shell's feed, to the page in the browser.
wiki_live_change_detail: A form or a command changes a record in a `db.transaction`: a planner plans an order, say, through `transitionOrder()`.
wiki_live_log_detail: In the same transaction, `recordActivity(tx, entry)` writes the activity entry (action, subject, before and after). Once the transaction commits, it announces the change; one rolled back logs and announces nothing.
wiki_live_feed_title: The shell's feed tells the tab
wiki_live_feed_detail: Each shell keeps one live query open per tab (the office's `watchTenantChanges`, built on `liveFeed(types, feedFor())`). It hears the announcement, keeps the changes to records the viewer may read, and sends them down its stream.
wiki_live_refresh_detail: `provideChangeFeed()` in the shell's layout hands each change to the components that follow its record: `refreshOnRecordChange()` refreshes their query, and the page shows the new data. There is no live query per record.
wiki_list_simplified: (simplified: no URL state, no saved views)
wiki_lifecycle_diagram: The order lifecycle: its statuses, and the moves between them coloured by who makes them.
wiki_lifecycle_choose: Choose a status to see how an order leaves it, how it gets there, and who makes each move.
wiki_lifecycle_caption: Drawn from `orderTransitions`; the office's moves by hand show around the status you choose.
wiki_gate_list: The gates, and what each does with a call by: {caller}
wiki_gate_developers_unless: Unless the caller's email is in the list: then it is admitted.
wiki_gate_caption: A module's own set (made with `moduleRemote`) adds the module check to one of these.
wiki_gate_members_admits: A signed-in member of the organization who isn't a field engineer: the office.
wiki_gate_managers_admits: An owner or admin of the organization.
wiki_gate_engineers_admits: A user linked to an engineer record.
wiki_gate_customers_admits: A customer's contact, linked to one of the organization's customers.
wiki_gate_customers_for: The customer portal; handlers scope every query to that customer and its sites.
wiki_gate_any_role_admits: Any member of the organization, field engineers and customers' contacts too.
wiki_gate_any_role_for: What every shell needs, such as the app shell's tenant.
wiki_gate_users_admits: Anyone signed in, with or without an organization.
wiki_gate_users_for: Functions that touch no tenant data.
wiki_gate_developers_admits: A signed-in user whose email is in DEVELOPER_EMAILS, across tenants.
wiki_gate_developers_for: The bug reports' pages. A 404 for everyone else.
wiki_gate_anyone_for: What is public on purpose: signing in, the theme, an invitation's link.

wiki_records_diagram: Records: a customer has sites, units and orders; a site has locations and units; a unit may be at a location; orders are about units; an engineer is assigned to orders.
wiki_tenancy_refused: Order {id} is {owner}'s, so for {tenant} it doesn't exist: `idInTenant()` found nothing, and the page answers as for an id no one has.
wiki_tenancy_leak: {tenant} reads {orders} of another tenant's. Ids are global; only the scope keeps a tenant to its own rows.
wiki_tenancy_diagram: The order table both tenants share, and the rows {tenant}'s query reads of it.
